module_title: Partnership & Sale of Goods: Foundational Concepts
introduction: This foundational level introduces the bedrock principles of commercial business structures and transactions. It details what legally constitutes a Partnership, the all-important 'True Test' of mutual agency, and differentiates a completed Sale from a mere Agreement to Sell.

core_concepts.title: Definition of Partnership (Section 4, IPA 1932)
core_concepts.description:
Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
- Persons entering into it are individually called 'Partners' and collectively a 'Firm'.
- Maximum Limit: The Partnership Act does not specify a maximum limit, but the Companies Act, 2013 (Section 464) limits a partnership firm to 50 members. Exceeding this makes it an 'Illegal Association'.

core_concepts.title: The True Test of Partnership: Mutual Agency (Section 6)
core_concepts.description:
Sharing of profits is a prima facie evidence of partnership, but it is NOT the conclusive test. (e.g., An employee getting a share of profits as a bonus is not a partner).
- The Conclusive Test: 'Mutual Agency'. The business must be carried on by all or any of them acting for all. Every partner is both an **Agent** (can bind other partners by his acts) and a **Principal** (is bound by the acts of other partners).
- Landmark Case: *Cox v. Hickman (1860)* established that mutual agency, not profit-sharing, is the true test of a partnership.

core_concepts.title: Sale vs. Agreement to Sell (Section 4, SoGA 1930)
core_concepts.description:
A Contract of Sale of Goods is a contract whereby the seller transfers or agrees to transfer the property (ownership) in goods to the buyer for a price.
- Sale: Where the transfer of property (ownership) in the goods takes place *immediately*. It creates a right *in rem* (against the whole world).
- Agreement to Sell: Where the transfer of ownership is to take place at a *future time* or subject to some *condition*. It creates a right *in personam* (only against the specific person).

core_concepts.title: Conditions and Warranties (Section 12, SoGA 1930)
core_concepts.description:
Not all terms in a contract of sale hold equal weight.
- Condition (Sec 12(2)): A stipulation **essential** to the main purpose of the contract. If breached, the aggrieved party has the right to completely **repudiate (cancel) the contract** and claim damages.
- Warranty (Sec 12(3)): A stipulation **collateral** (secondary) to the main purpose. If breached, the aggrieved party can ONLY claim **damages**, but cannot reject the goods or cancel the contract.

important_entities.name: Meaning of 'Goods' (Section 2(7), SoGA)
important_entities.key_fact: Goods means every kind of MOVABLE property.
important_entities.significance: The Sale of Goods Act applies strictly to movable property. It explicitly EXCLUDES actionable claims and money. It explicitly INCLUDES stock, shares, growing crops, grass, and things attached to the earth which are agreed to be severed before sale.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If A gives B his car in exchange for B's tractor, is it a Sale under SoGA? **NO**. A sale absolutely requires 'Price' (money consideration). If goods are exchanged for goods, it is a 'Barter', which is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, not the Sale of Goods Act.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Profit is a Hint; Agency is the Proof
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Sharing profits merely hints at a partnership, but the ability to bind each other legally (Mutual Agency) proves it.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'What is the true and conclusive test of a partnership?', unconditionally select **Mutual Agency** (or reference *Cox v. Hickman*).
